title: 2026-05-08-poc-readiness-corridor-access-lag-triage
summary: Weekly POC check-in focusing on access delays to staging gateway, KV-cache warmup anomalies, and latency variability across token sizes. Agreed to run a short load bench with pinned model variant, Redwood to provide benchmark matrix and creds checklist. Next steps: triage gateway timeouts, schedule focused benchmark window, Redwood to share limited perf-run script and docs.
topics: KV cache warmup and prefix caching
Pilot success criteria and next milestone
action_items: Ethan Park: Share bench matrix CSV and trimmed perf-run script by 2026-05-10
Maya Singh: Provide quick runbook for KV cache priming and a small test harness by 2026-05-11
Marcus Reid: Provide logs from staging gateway (connect timeouts) — due 2026-05-09
Leah Chen: Confirm success criteria for pilot (latency p95 <= 400ms, error rate < 0.2%) by 2026-05-12
next_steps: Redwood to send credentials checklist and bench script
Customer to run 30-minute controlled bench during 2026-05-11 09:00-09:30 PT window
Follow-up deep-dive on KV cache behaviour if bench shows cache miss rate > 20%
Schedule security docs handoff (SOC2 summary + audit logs) the week of 5/18
transcript:
Header: 2026-05-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46 minutes | Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Sofia (GreenGrid), Marcus, Leah

[00:00] Ethan: alright, everyone, thanks for hopping on. uh this is the weekly poc check-in for GreenGrid. main goals today — access hiccups, latency trend, and next bench window.
[00:18] Sofia: hey thanks, yea we've seen a bunch of small timeouts hitting our staging gateway, kinda intermittent, so wanted to sync.
[00:25] Marcus: yeah for context, our staging sits in eu-west-1 but some of the calls route through a central proxy. we saw a connection reset at the start of the run yesterday.
[00:36] Maya: quick clarifying q — are those connection resets 4xx auth or more tcp level?
[00:40] Marcus: mostly tcp, so like dial timeout then reset. sometimes 502s. we think it's a keepalive timing mismatch.
[00:48] Ethan: okay good, thanks. last week Maya gave the KV prime script, did you try it?
[00:54] Sofia: we ran it but results were odd — the model seemed cold for a while, like the prefix cache didn't stick, we saw heavy tail p95s for first 50 requests.
[01:04] Maya: hmm, could be our traffic shape, or you might be hitting a different model variant. did you pin model version in the request header?
[01:12] Marcus: we thought we were, but the gateway layers do some rewrites so maybe it fell back to a smaller quantized variant — we saw requests labeled 'Redwood Dedicate small' in the trace which might be mis-typed.
[01:24] Ethan: right, okay that naming noise happens; we'll send an explicit header example.
[01:29] Leah: also, a question on data retention — we need to know which logs will be forwarded to our SIEM, we have compliance folks asking.
[01:36] Maya: we can provide a logging map; for hosted we'll show you audit log fields, for dedicated the customer controls KMS and log export. i'll attach the SOC2 summary next email.
[01:45] Sofia: great, thanks. on latency — our recent run shows p50 ~120ms but p95 spikes to 760ms for longer prompts (~1k tokens), which is higher than our goal.
[01:57] Ethan: are you using batching in the test harness? batching affect tail latencies.
[02:01] Marcus: minimal batching, mostly single-stream calls to replicate product traffic.
[02:05] Maya: for single-stream with long sequences, we sometimes recommend a different kernel path — also quant profile matters. if you can share token length distribution we can suggest model+quant pairs.
[02:16] Sofia: i'll paste distribution after call.
[02:19] Ethan: ok let's move to bench plan — we'd like to run a controlled bench with pinned model, single-stream and batch profiles, and capture KV cache hit/miss metrics.
[02:29] Leah: timeline? we could do a 30-minute window on Monday morning.
[02:33] Ethan: how about 2026-05-11 09:00 PT?
[02:36] Marcus: works for infra.
[02:38] Maya: i'll provide a small perf-run script that warms prefixes and toggles batch sizes, and a CSV matrix for parameters.
[02:45] Sofia: perfect.
[02:48] Speaker 1: [inaudible]
[02:52] Ethan: there's also a mystery around cache warmup — we saw indicators that KV cache didn't persist across pods during a recent redeploy. did you do any rolling restarts?
[03:03] Marcus: yes we did a rolling restart yesterday overnight, might've flushed pods' local caches. we were expecting prefix caching to be retained in shared cache but it didn't.
[03:12] Maya: that suggests you might be on a config that uses local KV per pod, not centralized — we have a mode that stores shared KV in a stateful cache layer. i'll check your config.
[03:21] Leah: if switching to shared cache helps warmup, does that add cost?
[03:25] Maya: marginal, it's mostly a memory overhead on the service side. it's a tradeoff: lower cold-start latency vs small infra allocation.
[03:33] Sofia: acceptable if it stabilizes p95.
[03:36] Marcus: one more infra note — our NLB timeouts are default 350s, but the gateway has shorter keepalive. wonder if any mismatch there.
[03:46] Ethan: good call. Marcus can you capture exact proxy timeouts and share?
[03:50] Marcus: will do.
[03:52] Sophia: (laughs) small typo, i'm Sofia not Sophia.
[03:55] Ethan: noted — sorry Sofia.
[03:57] Maya: moving on to access — we still have a small blocker: service account for the connector hasn't propagated to the staging cluster, the token rotates every 24 hours so the short-lived creds expired during last run.
[04:10] Marcus: that's on us, we've been waiting for the SAML mapping to finish. expecting it today.
[04:14] Leah: how critical is the exact role mapping? can we use a temporary key to still run the bench?
[04:19] Ethan: yes temporary keys are fine — but send them through the credentials checklist so we avoid leaking. we'll delete keys after the run.
[04:26] Sofia: ok we'll do temp key today.
[04:29] Maya: on another note, you mentioned audit concerns — we can enable export of request/response metadata without storing payloads. that should satisfy most compliance asks.
[04:39] Leah: good. could we get an example schema of logs?
[04:42] Ethan: i'll attach the schema and the SOC2 one-pager.
[04:45] [05:00] Ethan: quick poll — are we comfortable with the success criteria as defined in the doc (p95 < 400ms, error rate < 0.2%)?
[05:08] Leah: those look right, may want to add a stability threshold over 24h but for the POC the 30-minute bench is fine.
[05:15] Sofia: agree.
[05:17] Marcus: one risk — if the gateway timeouts persist, we won't get clean bench runs.
[05:22] Maya: to mitigate, we can run the bench from a co-located host or use Redwood's dedicated test runner to bypass the customer proxy for that window.
[05:31] Ethan: do you want us to run the bench remotely?
[05:34] Marcus: prefer local, but if it's faster to isolate variables we can do Redwood-run first.
[05:39] Leah: timeline wise, let's try local run first on Monday; if failures happen, Redwood can run from your side as a follow-up.
[05:48] Ethan: sounds good.
[05:50] Maya: i'll also instrument additional KV metrics — miss rate, avg ttl, and a per-prefix hit rate, those should help root cause warmup issues.
[06:00] Sofia: that would be super helpful.
[06:03] [06:10] Ethan: security question from procurement — who owns keys in private deployment vs dedicated?
[06:16] Maya: in private (VPC/on-prem) customer owns KMS/HSM. in dedicated it's customer-controlled KMS integration but we keep platform-level audit. i'll send a short table.
[06:26] Leah: thanks.
[06:28] Marcus: quick ask — can we throttle token generation during bench to mimic product qps? we want to match 30 req/s bursts.
[06:36] Maya: yes bench script will support variable qps and dynamic batch sizes.
[06:41] Ethan: ok wrapping up, recap of owners — Ethan will send bench matrix and creds checklist; Maya sends perf script and KV runbook; Marcus will share gateway logs and NLB timeout values; Leah confirms success criteria by Tue.
[06:56] Sofia: noted.
[07:00] Ethan: any other blockers or questions?
[07:04] Leah: curious about model variants — is there a recommended default for 1k token workloads?
[07:09] Maya: for that length we recommend the medium-latency profile with quant q4f16 or similar; i'll specify exact variant names in the doc.
[07:18] Marcus: fine.
[07:20] Ethan: great. we'll reconvene after the bench — propose 2026-05-12 to review results.
[07:27] Leah: works. thanks everyone.
[07:30] Ethan: thanks, bye.

End Notes: occasional mis-transcriptions in product names (eg "Redwood Dedicate") noted; refer to attached bench matrix and logs for exact traces.
